text.p: These are the leading stories in Saturday's Pakistani newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said his landmark talks with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in the Maldives were a first step in putting bilateral dialogue on the right track.
- Three working groups are likely to be formed soon after the secretary level talks between India and Pakistan scheduled in Islamabad in the next few weeks, diplomatic sources said.

- At least a dozen workers of Sunni militant Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan were injured in Rawalpindi when police resorted to teargas shelling and baton charge to disperse demonstrators protesting against the arrest of their leader Azam Tariq.
- Pakistan has threatened to terminate its contract with Hubco, the country's largest private power producer, following a dispute over a broken measuring equipment.
- Pakistan has finalised negotiations with Turkmenistan for building two oil and gas pipelines at a cost of $4.5 billion.
- Four men in police uniforms looted foreign currency amounting to over 50 million rupees at the Jinnah Airport Karachi from money changers, police said.
- The government has ruled out any extradition of U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency employee Ayaz Baloch to the United States, adding that he would be tried under national laws.
- The number of public limited companies registered with the Registrar of Companies declined by more than 50 percent in January-April 1997 against the same year-ago period.
- Japanese government and business leaders will arrive in Pakistan on May 23 to explore investment prospects.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has taken a new initiative to bring about peace in Afghanistan by convening a conference of foreign ministers of its five neighbouring countries.
- Turkmenistan had offered to sell electricity to Pakistan at about two U.S. cents per kilowat-hour, Pakistan's Water and Power Minister Nisar Ali said.

- The SITE Association of Industry is negotiating with an Australian firm to run the power distribution system in the industrial area of Karachi after bulk power purchase from the Karachi Electric Supply Corportaion at a single point.
THE NEWS
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif told the Punjab governemnt to crush sectarian elements and establish peace at all cost.
- The government denied asking the United States to withdraw three Drug Enforcement Agency officials stationed in Islamabad.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif plans to visit Bangladesh and Bhutan after the National Assembly budget session next month.
- Pakistan will get 35 more Main Battle Tanks (MBTs) from Ukraine in June this year.
THE NATION
- India has agreed to form a joint working group with Pakistan on Kashmir. This will be announced after the two foreign secretaries meet at the end of June.
- Pakistan will get financial assistance to the tune of $600 million from the Asian Development Bank besides a $270 million loan for capital markets.
THE MUSLIM
- Former prime minsiter Benazir Bhutto refuted charges of alleged involvement of her husband in a sex scandal and termed these as "mud-slinging" campaign against the party.
- The Anti-Narcotics Force in Peshawar recovered 15 kg of fine quality heroin from a vehicle near Gora Qabristan, Peshawar Cantonment, and arrested the driver.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
